### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, touching **9** documentable anchor(s).

**3** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/kernel/contracts/auth-service.mdx`  _(via AuthManager (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/kernel/services-checklist.mdx`  _(via AuthManager (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/permissions/authentication.mdx`  _(via AuthManager (symbol, a top-level class))_

⛔ **3** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-2.mdx`  _(via AuthManager (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-3.mdx`  _(via AuthManager (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-4.mdx`  _(via AuthManager (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `VALIDATION_FAILED (literal, 50 pages)`
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **21** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d44b5e3daa828f7402c182770d0c025e537ed726` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `2a913715ffb494d1361fab5b027bcc17b2c94603` — the merge of head `ba221aaa508ff6e65051119bf91fb1447f8a65b9` into base `d44b5e3daa828f7402c182770d0c025e537ed726`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 2a913715ffb494d1361fab5b027bcc17b2c94603 && git checkout 2a913715ffb494d1361fab5b027bcc17b2c94603
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin d44b5e3daa828f7402c182770d0c025e537ed726 ba221aaa508ff6e65051119bf91fb1447f8a65b9 && git checkout -B drift-repro d44b5e3daa828f7402c182770d0c025e537ed726 && git merge --no-ff ba221aaa508ff6e65051119bf91fb1447f8a65b9

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d44b5e3daa828f7402c182770d0c025e537ed726
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs d44b5e3daa828f7402c182770d0c025e537ed726` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `32d1f053b45c73a56452d3e2cb04547412acf69f`
Local-runs: none
Scope: .changeset/sso-discovery-public-hosts.md (declaration lines), packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager-before-hook.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/sso-discovery-companion-origins.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/sso-discovery-companion-origins.test.ts + packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/sso-sign-out-of-idp.ts and `@better-auth/sso` 1.7.12 (`discoverOIDCConfig`, `validateDiscoveryUrl`, `fetchOIDCEndpoint`, `assertEndpointResolvesPublic`, the `/sso/register` handler) and `@better-auth/core/utils/host` (cited code outside the diff: read, never reviewed). `content/docs/permissions/sso.mdx` is a prose face, left to the seat's ACCEPT.
Security-touching: yes

Inputs: no card (a no-card order); the PR body, file list and net diff against merge base `986a0f208c8`; the check-runs on this head; the dev evidence on this head. Narrowing face: no `hits`, the whole diff outside the prose face is the floor.

Check-runs on this head, read once: every completed run is `success` or `skipped`, none failed. Test Core shards 1/10 to 10/10, TypeScript Type Check, Lint & Repo Gates, Dogfood Regression Gate, Build Core, Build Docs, Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard and the PR-body guards are `success`. The `Test Core` aggregate still read `in_progress` at the time of the read; the seat confirms it before any merge.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept set of `POST /sso/register`, narrowed — right.** An OIDC registration that reads a discovery document (no `skipDiscovery`), whose discovery URL is an http(s) URL on a public-looking name that the configured trusted origins do not list, and whose name resolves to at least one address `isPublicRoutableHost` refuses, was admitted to the vendor endpoint and is now refused `400 VALIDATION_FAILED` before it. Every other registration is answered as before. The narrowing makes real, at registration, the refusal the vendor already applies to the endpoints it reads at sign-in; it takes no declared capability away, because `OS_TRUSTED_ORIGINS` stays the declared way to register a provider on an internal network and the check returns before resolving for a configured origin.
- **The host resolved is the host the vendor reads — right.** `ssoRegisterDiscoveryRead` picks `oidcConfig.discoveryEndpoint`, else `computeDiscoveryUrl(issuer)`; the vendor's `discoverOIDCConfig` picks `existingConfig.discoveryEndpoint || computeDiscoveryUrl(issuer)` with the same function. The hook reads the body before the vendor's schema parse, and each divergence falls on the stricter side: a `skipDiscovery` that is not literally `true`, or a non-string `discoveryEndpoint`, is still resolved here and then refused by the vendor's schema. The vendor's register handler makes no other server-side read (SAML registration fetches nothing; redirects are refused, `redirect: "manual"`).
- **Why the check is not redundant — right.** The vendor fetches discovery only from a trusted origin (`validateDiscoveryUrl`) and skips its own resolution for a trusted origin (`assertEndpointResolvesPublic`), so once the body-named origins join the endpoint's trusted origins the vendor resolves nothing for that host. The diff resolves it first, against the configured predicate alone, and hands the body-named origins on only afterwards.
- **Body-named origins handed on only for an admitted actor — right, and a second narrowing.** At the merge base `ssoDiscoveryTrustedOrigins(body)` reached the context change for every request; now it stays `[]` unless the actor resolved, is not held and is a platform admin. A request with no resolved actor reaches the vendor with the configured trust plus the fixed companion table only, so its discovery URL is read only when the deployment lists it. No session still answers the vendor's `401`, and no name is resolved for it or for a refused non-admin (`403` is thrown first).
- **Early returns — right as a mirror of the vendor.** An address literal and a non-public name are not resolved: neither enters `ssoDiscoveryTrustedOrigins` (same predicate), so the vendor refuses them unless configured. A name that fails to resolve, an empty answer, and a runtime without `node:dns/promises` are left to the read, as `assertEndpointResolvesPublic` leaves them. Resolved addresses are judged by the same predicate, which unmaps IPv4-mapped IPv6 before classifying.
- **Public surface — right.** No package export moves (`sso-discovery-companion-origins.ts` is not re-exported from the package entry); no schema key, error code or stored row changes. `VALIDATION_FAILED` is plugin-auth's registered code. The bridge relays `400 SSO_REGISTER_FAILED`, pinned by a case.
- **The member the refusal names — wrong in one case, see S1.** The changeset and the PR body publish "refused on `issuer` (or `oidcConfig.discoveryEndpoint`)" without qualification.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/plugin-auth: patch`, with the bang, the **BREAKING** banner, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: none` and an ADR-0087 `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` disposition. This matches what the diff publishes: one runtime answer of an HTTP door is narrowed, no metadata author writes an SSO registration, so the kind is `none` and AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist step 3 sends a non-protocol breaking change to `patch` with its banner and disposition kept. The banner names the affected caller and the one-line fix (list the origin in `OS_TRUSTED_ORIGINS`). The `Clause-②:` line is the same on the PR body and the changeset, and `(narrowing)` is the correct arm. `Check Changeset` is `success` on this head.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev flag, ordering against the sign-out switch's own discovery read: answered in S1. The rule itself holds in either order.
- Dev flag, `@objectstack/core/egress` not reused: accepted for this PR. The stated reason (one rule and one way out at registration and at sign-in) is coherent with the code read.
- Dev flag, three gate families NOT MEASURED locally: `Lint & Repo Gates`, `Type Check · debt ledger` and the Test Core shards are `success` on this head, so CI measured them.
- Fixture triage (the sign-out update case re-seeded under a public answer): read; what the case pins is unchanged.
- SQL push-down: not applicable. The diff adds no query, no id materialisation and no in-app join.
- Private residuals held by the security seat: R1–R5 — graded in the seat's private notes. None is graded must-fix for this PR.

### ④ Design judgment

- **`sso-discovery-companion-origins.ts`** — holds. `refuseSsoDiscoveryHostNotPublic` reads `body` only, takes the configured predicate and an injectable resolver, and agrees clause by clause with the vendor's `assertEndpointResolvesPublic` (configured trust first, FQDN only, `lookup(all)`, every address judged). The refusal names the host, the member, the rule and the remedy. Tried and not broken: userinfo in the URL, numeric and bracketed literals (normalised to literals by URL parsing, left to the vendor's synchronous refusal), trailing-dot and metadata names (the shared predicate), a mixed public and private answer (refused), an explicit endpoint on another host than the issuer's (that host is the one resolved), a redirecting discovery host (the vendor refuses redirects).
- **`auth-manager-before-hook.ts`** — holds on the rule; one ordering finding. The check runs inside the admitted-actor block, after the platform-admin, held-actor and domain gates, and `bodyOrigins` is assigned only after it.
  - **S1 (should-fix) — with `signOutOfIdp: true`, the refusal does not come from the new check.** `assertSsoSignOutOfIdpSupported` runs first and reads the same discovery URL through the vendor's `fetchDiscoveryDocument` under the configured trust; for a host that resolves to a non-public address that read is refused by the vendor's own resolution, and the hook answers `400 VALIDATION_FAILED` on `signOutOfIdp` with the vendor's error text relayed verbatim. The rule holds (nothing is read from the host), but the member is not `issuer` / `oidcConfig.discoveryEndpoint` as the changeset and PR body publish, the message is not the one this diff wrote (which by its own acceptance note names the host and the remedy and not the resolved address), and the name is resolved by a path other than the one the new describe pins. The pre-existing case "on register, its discovery read keeps the configured trust" pins `field: 'signOutOfIdp'` for exactly this input, so the suite currently holds the two answers apart. Fix: call `refuseSsoDiscoveryHostNotPublic` before `assertSsoSignOutOfIdpSupported` on the register branch and add the switch-on case to the new describe, or qualify the published member in the changeset. Either is a few lines; neither changes which registrations are admitted.
- **`auth-manager.ts`** — a jsdoc hunk only; it agrees with the code (`ssoDiscoveryTrustedOrigins` judges by name, the register door resolves before handing the list on).
- **`sso-discovery-companion-origins.test.ts`** — holds. The integration describe drives the real register door and the bridge with a `node:dns/promises` double and a fetch recorder, and asserts all three of status and member, nothing fetched from the host, and no row; the controls (public answer registers and fetches exactly the discovery URL, configured origin registers on a private answer, no session answers `401` and asks no name) keep the refusals from being vacuous. The unit describe pins which host is resolved and every early return. The ablation evidence (7 of 42 red with the hook at the merge base) shows the cases bind to the hook change.
  - **N1 (nit)** — no case pins a non-admin session (`403`) asking no name; the code order guarantees it today.
  - **N2 (nit)** — the module jsdoc says the register endpoint's discovery read is "the one server-side read"; true of the vendor endpoint, while the hook's sign-out check makes a second read of the same URL when the switch is on. One clause would say so.
- **`.changeset/sso-discovery-public-hosts.md` declaration lines** — correct, see ②; the member sentence is covered by S1.

No must-fix. One should-fix (S1), two nits.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `ba221aaa508ff6e65051119bf91fb1447f8a65b9`
Local-runs: none
Scope: .changeset/sso-discovery-public-hosts.md (declaration lines), packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager-before-hook.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/sso-discovery-companion-origins.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/sso-discovery-companion-origins.test.ts + packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/sso-sign-out-of-idp.ts and `@better-auth/sso` 1.7.12 (`discoverOIDCConfig`, `validateDiscoveryUrl`, `fetchOIDCEndpoint`, `assertEndpointResolvesPublic`, the `/sso/register` handler) and `@better-auth/core/utils/host` (cited code outside the diff: read, never reviewed). `content/docs/permissions/sso.mdx` is a prose face, left to the seat's ACCEPT.
Security-touching: yes

Delta review. This head is one commit over `32d1f053b45`, the head of record 7026276533, whose judgments stand for everything that commit does not touch; the commit was read in full (four files: the before-hook, the module jsdoc, the test file, the docs page) and the whole-PR diff against merge base `986a0f208c8` still names the same six files. Inputs: no card (a no-card order); the PR's diff; the check-runs on this head; the dev evidence on this head.

Check-runs on this head, read twice: 40 `success`, 17 `skipped`, none failed. Two were `in_progress` at both reads, `Check Changeset` and `PR-body guards (claim · duplicate · Part-of · single-writer path)`; the seat confirms both before any merge. Test Core, type check, lint and the Dogfood Regression Gate are `success`.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept set of `POST /sso/register` — unchanged by the delta, right.** The commit moves one call. Which registrations are admitted is the same as on the prior head: both checks must pass, in either order.
- **The member a refusal names, with `signOutOfIdp: true` — changed, right.** A registration that reads a discovery document from a host resolving to a non-public address is now refused `400 VALIDATION_FAILED` on `issuer` (or `oidcConfig.discoveryEndpoint`) with this diff's own message, whatever the switch says. On the prior head it was refused on `signOutOfIdp` with the vendor's text. The changeset's unqualified member sentence is now true for every registration that reads a discovery document.
- **Order of the register branch, read on the tree — right.** `resolveActor` → `assertActorNotHeld` → platform-admin (`403 SSO_REGISTER_FORBIDDEN`) → `assertSsoProviderDomainFree` → `refuseSsoDiscoveryHostNotPublic` → `assertSsoSignOutOfIdpSupported` → `bodyOrigins = ssoDiscoveryTrustedOrigins(body)`. Only the last-but-one pair swapped. The identity, held-actor, platform-admin and domain gates keep their places, and `bodyOrigins` is still assigned last, inside the admitted-actor block.
- **One answer that moved with the order — right, and worth knowing.** A registration with the switch on that fails both the public-host rule and the sign-out capability rule (for instance a document naming no logout endpoint) now gets the public-host refusal first. That is the intended precedence.
- **Side effect of the sign-out check now sits behind the rule — right.** The logout endpoint that check keeps for the after-hook is recorded only for a request the public-host rule admitted.
- **Public surface — unchanged.** No export, schema key, error code or stored row moves in the delta.

### ② Semver level

Unchanged and still correct: `@objectstack/plugin-auth: patch`, with the bang, the **BREAKING** banner, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: none` and the ADR-0087 `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` disposition. The delta does not touch the changeset, and it removes the one case in which the changeset's member sentence was inexact. `Check Changeset` was still `in_progress` on this head at the time of the read (it was `success` on the prior head with the same changeset); the seat confirms it.

### ③ Boundary flags

- S1 of record 7026276533 (ordering against the sign-out switch's own discovery read): answered by the reorder, see ④.
- N1 and N2 of that record: answered, see ④.
- SQL push-down: not applicable. The delta adds no query, no id materialisation and no in-app join.
- Private residuals held by the security seat: R1–R5 — graded in the seat's private notes. None is graded must-fix for this PR.

### ④ Design judgment

- **`auth-manager-before-hook.ts`** — S1 resolved. `refuseSsoDiscoveryHostNotPublic` is called before `assertSsoSignOutOfIdpSupported`, and the comment says why. Both functions choose the discovery URL the same way for a register body (`oidcConfig.discoveryEndpoint`, else the issuer's well-known URL through the vendor's `computeDiscoveryUrl`), so the host the sign-out check reads is the host the rule just resolved. Tried and not broken: the reorder leaves no path on which the body-named origins reach the vendor before the rule ran, and none on which the sign-out read precedes it for a registration that reads a discovery document.
- **`sso-discovery-companion-origins.test.ts`** — holds. The pre-existing switch-on register case now pins `field: 'issuer'`; a new case in the rule's own describe pins the same with the name asked, nothing fetched from the host and no row; the update-provider case still pins `signOutOfIdp`, which is correct, since the rule is a registration rule. The ordering ablation (2 of 44 red with the old hook, both the switch-on cases) shows these two bind to the order. N1 is done: a `403 SSO_REGISTER_FORBIDDEN` control asserts no name asked and nothing fetched.
- **`sso-discovery-companion-origins.ts`** — N2 done: the jsdoc now says the vendor's endpoint makes no other read and names the sign-out check's read of the same document.
  - **N3 (nit)** — "only after `refuseSsoDiscoveryHostNotPublic` has admitted its host" is exact for a registration that reads a discovery document. With `oidcConfig.skipDiscovery` and the switch on, the rule resolves nothing (the registration reads none) and the sign-out check still reads the document, under the configured trust and the vendor's own resolution; that registration is refused on `signOutOfIdp`, as before this PR. The rule holds there; the jsdoc clause and the docs sentence "refused on the same member" are each one qualifier short. No case pins this combination.
- **`auth-manager.ts`** and the **changeset declaration lines** — untouched by the delta; the prior record's judgment stands.
- **`content/docs/permissions/sso.mdx`** — prose face, not reviewed here. Noted for the seat only: the headline now states what the registration checks before reading, which is the claim the code supports.

No must-fix, no should-fix. One nit (N3).
